standard.title: Methods for Civic Participation
standard.description: explain the methods or strategies related to making decisions about civic participation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have examined ways citizens can participate in democracy (AC9HC7K02) and can assess possible effects of actions and evaluate perspectives (AC9HS6S06). The Y7 capability shift is to explain the methods and strategies of civic participation — understanding how and why particular participation strategies are chosen, not just what they are.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the methods and strategies of civic participation, identifying how these contribute to democratic and just outcomes.

nodes.label: Features of civic participation methods
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain the features of different civic participation methods — including their mechanisms, reach, and intended outcomes.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three civic participation methods (e.g. petition, social media campaign, direct action) and describe the key features of each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain the features of civic participation methods including social media campaigns, letters, petitions, participation in mediation or tribunals, and direct action; describe how each method works and what makes it appropriate for different civic goals.
wider: Investigate historical examples of each civic participation method (e.g. a successful petition campaign, a landmark tribunal case) to understand how the method works in practice
Compare civic participation methods available in Australia with those in a country with fewer democratic freedoms to appreciate the significance of participatory rights
Explore how digital tools have created new forms of civic participation (e.g. online petitions, social media campaigns) and evaluate how these differ from traditional methods
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a clear understanding of what each method involves and how it works, students cannot reason about which method is appropriate for a given civic goal — which is the core capability this descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Students need a working repertoire of participation methods with genuine knowledge of how each works — not just a list of names. Practise describing what each method involves before moving to strategic reasoning about selection.

success_criteria: Identify at least three civic participation methods and describe the key features of each
Explain what makes a particular method appropriate for a specific type of civic goal

nodes.label: Responsibilities of active citizenship
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the core responsibilities of active citizenship and evaluate how citizens enacting democratic values contribute to a cohesive society.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two responsibilities associated with active citizenship (e.g. staying informed, contributing to community, participating in democratic processes) and explain how they contribute to democratic life.
nodes.typical_width: Identify the core responsibilities of active citizenship; evaluate how the contributions of citizens who enact democratic values (e.g. through disability advocacy services, Landcare groups, community organisations) demonstrate active citizenship and contribute to social cohesion; connect individual action to broader democratic outcomes.
wider: Investigate a specific community organisation or advocacy group (e.g. Landcare, disability advocacy services) and evaluate the contribution it makes to both local community and democratic participation
Examine what is meant by 'civic responsibility' in different cultural contexts — are the responsibilities of citizenship understood differently across communities?
Explore First Nations Australian conceptions of responsibility to community and Country as a form of active citizenship that predates colonial democratic institutions

response_modes.reason: Examining diverse examples of active citizenship (disability advocacy, environmental action, First Nations community organisations) helps students understand that active citizenship takes many forms and is not limited to formal political participation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Exploring First Nations conceptions of community responsibility as a form of civic engagement offers a genuinely different frame for understanding what 'active citizenship' means — one grounded in relational and land-based responsibilities rather than individual political action.
success_criteria: Identify at least two responsibilities of active citizenship and explain how they support democratic life
Give an example of active citizenship contributing to social cohesion and explain the connection

nodes.label: Choosing participation strategies for civic goals
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how participation methods and strategies are linked to specific civic goals, identifying why certain methods are chosen to achieve democratic and just outcomes.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain why a given civic participation method (e.g. a petition, a social media campaign, a direct action) would be chosen for a particular civic goal, identifying the connection between method and intended outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and evaluate the methods and actions linked to active and informed citizenship; explain how citizens and groups choose methods to achieve democratic and just outcomes in local, national, regional and global contexts; connect participation strategy to civic purpose (e.g. raising awareness vs creating legal change vs applying community pressure).
wider: Investigate a real civic campaign (e.g. heritage building preservation, green space protection, environmental advocacy) and analyse the participation strategies used and why they were effective or ineffective
Compare the participation strategies chosen by two different groups seeking the same civic outcome — evaluating which strategies were more effective and why
Design a civic participation strategy for a hypothetical local issue, justifying the choice of methods against the civic goal and the available participation options

response_modes.reason: This node integrates the repertoire of methods (N1) and the understanding of civic responsibilities (N2) into strategic reasoning about participation — students connect what methods are available with why a particular method serves a particular goal.

success_criteria: Explain why a particular civic participation method would be chosen for a specific civic goal
Identify the connection between participation strategy and intended democratic or just outcome
